subject: Mutual Action Plan — Technical evaluation kickoff & benchmark criteria
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Li <alex.li@clarahealth.com>, Evan Brooks <evan.b@clarahealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Mutual Action Plan — Technical evaluation kickoff & benchmark criteria

Hi Alex / Evan —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Per our discussion I captured a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on the technical evaluation milestone so we can get the benchmark running next week. I attached a one-tab MAP and a prompt set for the eval. High-level items below; please review and flag anything you'd like adjusted.

Summary (what we agreed would be tested)
- Purpose: Measure model latency, cost, and response quality on Clara Health’s triage & summarization flows so you can pick a production configuration.
- Scope: 500 real-world prompts (provided by Clara), 3 candidate model families, both single-request latency (p95) and throughput at modest batch sizes.

Proposed benchmark success criteria (initial targets)
- Quality: human-eval pass rate >= 85% on our shared rubric (accuracy + helpfulness) OR automated semantic-similarity F1 >= 0.82 on extractive QA tests.
- Latency: p95 end-to-end generation latency <= 250 ms for 128-token responses; p95 <= 400 ms for 512-token responses (single-request).
- Cost: inference cost <= $0.30 per 1k output tokens (hosted config baseline) OR equivalent on Dedicated.
- Throughput: sustain 50 RPS with p95 latency < 350 ms in burst scenario (internal infra to validate).

Model shortlist to run in the first pass
- Llama-3-13B (instruction-tuned) — good quality/latency balance
- Mistral-Instruct-7B — low-cost baseline for instruction tasks
- Falcon-40B-Instruct — higher-capacity variant to evaluate headroom

Ownership & timeline (draft)
- Clara: provide 500-prompt test set, acceptance criteria signoff, and security contact (due 2026-02-23). Owner: Alex Li.
- Redwood: run benchmarks, surface p95/cost tradeoffs, provide raw logs & result deck. Owner: Monica Patel. Target run start: 2026-02-24.
- Redwood Sales: finalize MAP and review procurement schedule. Owner: Connor O'Brien. Target close (tentative): 2026-03-12.

Dependencies
- NDA / data sharing access (we agreed to use pseudonymized prompts)
- Access to any sample traffic patterns you want us to simulate
- A short list of production latency SLOs from your infra team if different from the targets above

Attachments included: MAP_ClaraHealth_v1.xlsx (milestones & owners), benchmark-prompt-set.csv (example prompts), scope-and-timeline.pdf

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm the timeline and that Alex will share the 500 prompts by Mon 2/23.
2) Monica will schedule the benchmark window and share an execution plan by EOD Mon 2/23.
3) We lock the final model shortlist after your feedback on quality vs cost tradeoffs.

If that all looks good I'll mark the MAP as draft-final and kick off scheduling with Monica.

Thanks,
Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
(redwood.com)

Thanks — I have the plan and the slot reserved. Quick execution notes: 

Execution plan (summary)
- Run window: Tue 2026-02-24 09:00-13:00 PST (we reserved capacity on a mix of Dedicated and hosted nodes to compare).
- Instance types & config: 2 x a100-like nodes for Falcon-40B, 1 x 80GB GPU for Llama-3-13B, and 2 x 40GB quantized runners for Mistral & Redwood-2-6B to simulate low-cost paths. Batch sizes: 1, 4, 8 for single-request and burst measurements.
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, per-request token counts, model output diffs, per-1k-token cost estimate, and raw logs (traces & KV cache stats).
- Quality evaluation: automated semantic-similarity scoring against ground truth + 40-item human spot-check (we'll sample across prompt categories).

Deliverables and timing
- Raw results + cost/latency deck: Wed 2026-02-25 morning (we'll upload to the Drive link and notify).
- Shortlist recommendation + tradeoffs: Wed 2026-02-25 EOD.

Need from Clara: the 500-prompt CSV in the same format as benchmark-prompt-set.csv (column headers: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_summary, category). Please also share any simulated traffic pattern files if you want throughput tuning.

I'll upload the execution plan doc and the run script snippet to the shared Drive by EOD today.

Monica Patel
Technical Program Manager | Redwood Inference
